🌎 BEYOND THE 956

HILLSBOROUGH COUNTY, Fla. — A 74-year-old blind Florida man charged with first-degree murder stunned a courtroom during jury selection when he offered to plead guilty and accept life in prison — in exchange for a Philly cheesesteak, fries and a Pepsi.

Robert Kessler is charged with first-degree murder and abuse of a dead body in connection with the 2021 death of Stephanie Crone-Overholt, 47, according to reports on the case. He has been in custody since 2021 and was representing himself at trial, reports said.

During a court appearance on Monday, October 26, Circuit Judge Nick Nazaretian told Kessler he could enter an open plea and receive life in prison, according to PEOPLE and the Sarasota Herald-Tribune. Kessler replied that he would do that for a Philly cheesesteak with onions and mayonnaise, an order of fries and a 20-ounce Pepsi, saying the deal would save taxpayers the cost of a lengthy trial.

The judge rejected the condition, telling Kessler he could not give food to people in exchange for a plea, though he could guarantee lunch that day. Kessler then withdrew the proposed plea and asked for jury selection to continue, reports said.

Crone-Overholt's dismembered remains were found by fishermen in McKay Bay near Tampa in November 2021, according to reports. The trial continued this week, according to the Herald-Tribune.

The charges against Kessler are allegations, and he is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post; PEOPLE; Sarasota Herald-Tribune.
